_comment: Published DENSE top-1, for the parity gate in 02_dense_baselines.
Transcribed from the sources named below and independently re-verified;
no value here was reconstructed from memory. A dense baseline below
these figures makes every "matches or exceeds dense" claim read as
"exceeds our undertrained dense", which is attack A1 in the plan.
tolerance is in absolute top-1 points.

resnet50/cifar10.source: GraNet, Liu et al., NeurIPS 2021, arXiv:2106.10404, Table 1
resnet50/cifar10.protocol: 160 epochs, batch 128, SGD(0.9) lr 0.1, x10 drop at [80,120], wd 5e-4
resnet50/cifar10.note: Printed identically in GraNet Tables 1, 2, 6 and 9 -- four-way internal agreement.

resnet50/cifar100.source: GraNet, Liu et al., NeurIPS 2021, arXiv:2106.10404, Table 1
resnet50/cifar100.protocol: 160 epochs, batch 128, SGD(0.9) lr 0.1, x10 drop at [80,120], wd 5e-4

vgg19/cifar10.source: GraNet, Liu et al., NeurIPS 2021, arXiv:2106.10404, Table 1
vgg19/cifar10.protocol: 160 epochs, batch 128, SGD(0.9) lr 0.1, x10 drop at [80,120], wd 5e-4
vgg19/cifar10.note: GraSP (arXiv:2002.07376) reports 94.23 for VGG19/CIFAR-10 with no std. The two differ; GraNet is preferred here because it reports a std and because its sparse numbers are the ones being compared against.

vgg19/cifar100.source: GraNet, Liu et al., NeurIPS 2021, arXiv:2106.10404, Table 1
vgg19/cifar100.protocol: 160 epochs, batch 128, SGD(0.9) lr 0.1, x10 drop at [80,120], wd 5e-4
vgg19/cifar100.note: GraSP reports 74.16, again with no std.

resnet34/cifar10.note: NO published dense ResNet-34/CIFAR-10 baseline was located. GraNet covers ResNet-20/ResNet-50/VGG-19 only, and EAST reports no dense row. This is the ladder ANCHOR cell, so its dense parity cannot be checked against the literature -- state that as a limitation rather than borrowing a figure from a different architecture.
